label: Higher softmax temperature → sharper distribution
description:
Some learners flip the relationship between temperature and distribution sharpness. Higher temperature actually FLATTENS the softmax (more uniform, more random sampling); lower temperature SHARPENS it (more peaked, more deterministic). The intuition: T appears in the denominator inside the exp, so larger T shrinks the differences between logits.

A quick check: T → 0 means argmax (deterministic). T → ∞ means uniform.
probeQuestions: If you raise the temperature in softmax sampling, does the model become more deterministic or more random?
What happens to the softmax output as temperature → 0?
correctionPromptTemplate: The learner believes higher temperature sharpens the softmax. Walk them through the math: softmax(x_i / T) — show what happens at T=0.1 vs T=10 with concrete logits. Don't dump the answer; ask a calibrated question first.
